title: Svalbard - The Seed Vault, Quietly Leaking

target.note: short declaratives, one idea per beat. Little to no pause between sentences.

narration:
Beneath an Arctic mountain, the world's seeds sleep.
This is the Svalbard Global Seed Vault.
It opened in 2008, on a Norwegian island.
A long tunnel runs down into the rock.
The rock there is permafrost, frozen for millennia.
The vault is cut straight into that ice.
Above the doorway, the midsummer sun barely rises.
Down inside, the seeds sleep in the cold.
The seeds are packed into small foil packets.
Around a million samples, from a hundred nations.
Wheat, rice, barley, beans, and millet.
Every sample in there is a spare copy.
The original seed always stays on the farm.
Each nation's crop insurance, stored in a mountain.
Inside, the air holds at minus eighteen degrees.
That is colder than any farm freezer.
In that cold, the seeds sleep for centuries.
The original plan was simple: shut the door.
Then leave the whole vault to the ice.
Then, in 2016, the mountain began to leak.
Meltwater came in through the entrance tunnel.
Water at the door, in a frozen land.
The entrance flooded with eight hundred tonnes.
The staff were cut off for a year.
The seed samples themselves were never touched.
They lay above the waterline, in the cold.
The same permafrost that keeps it thaws too.
The vault is watched now, year round.
A new access tunnel is being built.
New lights on the snow, night and day.
It is still a bunker against catastrophe.
Catastrophe is already moving into the mountain.
The coldest air on earth is warming here.
The seeds are still fine, for now.
Somewhere under the snow, it is still seeping.

beats.line: Beneath an Arctic mountain, the world's seeds sleep.
beats.visual: wide flat arctic snowfield at night, white ground to the horizon; one small pale yellow wedge of light lying on the snow, tiny in a big empty frame

beats.line: This is the Svalbard Global Seed Vault.
beats.visual: hand-lettered 'SVALBARD GLOBAL SEED VAULT' stamped across the sky over the mountain; title card hold

beats.line: It opened in 2008, on a Norwegian island.
beats.visual: flat map of the north Atlantic with Norway picked out and one small island far above it; label 'SPITSBERGEN'

beats.line: A long tunnel runs down into the rock.
beats.visual: long straight entrance tunnel in one-point perspective, hand-drawn ribs overhead, receding into black; character small in it, walking away from us

beats.line: The rock there is permafrost, frozen for millennia.
beats.visual: cutaway of the mountain: layered rock and frozen ground drawn as dense vertical hatching; hand-lettered label 'PERMAFROST'

beats.line: The vault is cut straight into that ice.
beats.visual: the same cutaway with a straight rectangular hall carved into the frozen layer, lit warm from inside; character awed at the base of the frame

beats.line: Above the doorway, the midsummer sun barely rises.
beats.visual: the entrance doorway from outside at high summer; a low yellow sun just clearing the ridge, everything still white

beats.line: Down inside, the seeds sleep in the cold.
beats.visual: inside the cold room: metal shelving running out past both frame edges, stacked flat with foil packets

beats.line: The seeds are packed into small foil packets.
beats.visual: close on a hand holding one foil packet up to the light, a crop drawing stamped on the front

beats.line: Around a million samples, from a hundred nations.
beats.visual: the shelves receding into the dark; big hand-lettered number '1,000,000' stamped across the frame

beats.line: Wheat, rice, barley, beans, and millet.
beats.visual: five packets pulled forward in a row on one shelf, each stamped with a different crop drawing

beats.line: Every sample in there is a spare copy.
beats.visual: one packet in the vault beside one packet still in a field, drawn side by side; labels 'COPY' and 'ORIGINAL'

beats.line: The original seed always stays on the farm.
beats.visual: character close-up, flat mouth, one hand shading his eyes; speech bubble 'the original stays home'

beats.line: Each nation's crop insurance, stored in a mountain.
beats.visual: simple globe with hand-drawn continent shapes, small packet icons dotted over every continent

beats.line: Inside, the air holds at minus eighteen degrees.
beats.visual: a wall thermometer in the cold room; the mercury line far below zero; big number '-18 C'

beats.line: That is colder than any farm freezer.
beats.visual: an ordinary farm freezer door beside the vault's inner door, drawn side by side for scale

beats.line: In that cold, the seeds sleep for centuries.
beats.visual: one packet resting on a shelf, drawn very large, dust of frost on it; nothing else in shot

beats.line: The original plan was simple: shut the door.
beats.visual: the four heavy doors down the tunnel, receding; character drawing a plan of them on a clipboard

beats.line: Then leave the whole vault to the ice.
beats.visual: the tunnel doors shut, frost creeping across them, held dead centre and still

beats.line: Then, in 2016, the mountain began to leak.
beats.visual: wide cutaway of the whole mountain in grey, everything greyed out except one lit chamber; label '2008'

beats.line: Meltwater came in through the entrance tunnel.
beats.visual: the tunnel mouth from outside; a brown meltwater channel cutting through the snow straight at the door

beats.line: Water at the door, in a frozen land.
beats.visual: a wall of meltwater standing inside the entrance tunnel, the door half behind it, held and cold

beats.line: The entrance flooded with eight hundred tonnes.
beats.visual: hand-lettered number '800 TONNES' stamped over the flooded tunnel floor

beats.line: The staff were cut off for a year.
beats.visual: the entrance shut and barricaded, a lone figure on the snow above it, dwarfed; label '2016'

beats.line: The seed samples themselves were never touched.
beats.visual: character close-up, flat mouth, nodding once; speech bubble 'the seeds were fine'

beats.line: They lay above the waterline, in the cold.
beats.visual: cutaway: water pooled in the tunnel, the seed chamber drawn above it and dry, one clean line between

beats.line: The same permafrost that keeps it thaws too.
beats.visual: the same cutaway with the frozen layer drawn thin and ragged, melt arrows working into it; label 'AND MELTING'

beats.line: The vault is watched now, year round.
beats.visual: a small camera on a stalk above the tunnel door, and a red lamp lit on its side

beats.line: A new access tunnel is being built.
beats.visual: a fresh concrete tunnel mouth being cut into the hillside beside the old one, machinery drawn small

beats.line: New lights on the snow, night and day.
beats.visual: the snowfield at night again, two wedges of light now lying on the snow; character standing between them, small

beats.line: It is still a bunker against catastrophe.
beats.visual: character mid-frame, hands low, flat mouth, looking straight out at us; speech bubble 'a bunker'

beats.line: Catastrophe is already moving into the mountain.
beats.visual: a thin red line creeping across the mountain's snowline from below; nothing else changes in the frame

beats.line: The coldest air on earth is warming here.
beats.visual: the same arctic slope drawn a few shades warmer, bare grey rock showing through the snow; hand-lettered '-2.6 C PER DECADE'

beats.line: The seeds are still fine, for now.
beats.visual: character close-up, mouth a flat line, holding a single foil packet; speech bubble 'for now'

beats.line: Somewhere under the snow, it is still seeping.
beats.visual: under the snow, the mountain in cutaway, one slow dark line of water moving through the frozen layer; character tiny, awed, no label
